verses.1: And the children of Israel committed evil deeds in the eyes of Jehovah. And Ehud died.
verses.2: And Jehovah sold them into the hands of Yavin, the king of Kenaan. He ruled over the region, and his chief minister was Sisra. He ruled over those lands.
verses.3: And the children of Israel cried out to Jehovah, “Give us five thousand iron rings!” But he strengthened them, and they worked for him for forty years.
verses.4: And there was a woman who was a prophetess. She judged Israel at that time.
verses.5: And she sat under a fig tree, between the Ramah and Bet El on Mount Efraim. And the sons of Israel went to her for judgment.
verses.6: And she sent for Barak, son of Abinoam from Naphtali. She said to him, “Now, God, the Lord of Israel, has commanded you to go. You must take twelve thousand men from the people of Naphtali and from the people of Zebulun with you.”
verses.7: And I will bring them to the river Kishon. I will also bring with me Sisra, the charioteer Yavin, and his chariot. I will give them into your hands.
verses.8: And he said to her, “Barak, will you go with me? If you go with me, I will go. But if you don’t go with me, then I won’t go either.”
verses.9: And she said, “Let me go with you. But I refuse to walk along the path you are taking. For in the hands of a woman, Jehovah will sell Sisera. Then she got up and went away with Barak, the holy one.”
verses.10: And Barak cried out for Zebulun and Naphtali, the holy ones. He led twelve thousand men with him. And Deborah also went with him.
verses.11: And his companion, the kinist, separated from him right away. He left Moses’ tent and built his own shelter until the day of Kedosh.
verses.12: And they told Sisera that Barak son of Abinadab had taken control of Mount Tabor.
verses.13: And Sisera cried out to all his chariots. There were forty iron chariots in total. And all the people who were with him, those who had been brought from the various tribes, were also there. They went to the river Kishon.
verses.14: And Deborah said to Barak, “Arise! For today is the day when Jehovah has given Sisera into your hands. Now, Jehovah has come before you. Barak came down from Mount Tabor, along with twelve thousand men after him.”
verses.15: And Jehovah destroyed Sisra and all its chariots and all its camps, in front of Barak. Sisra fell from its chariot, and it died by its own feet.
verses.16: And Barak pursued the chariot and the camp until dawn. All of the camp of Sisera was destroyed by fire; not a single person survived.
verses.17: And Sisera walked with his feet toward the tent of Jael, the wife of Knehi. For peace was established between Jael and the king of Canaan, as well as between the house of Knehi.
verses.18: And Ya’el went out to meet Sisra. She said to him, “Surah Adonai, Surah Ely! Do not be afraid.” Then he removed the covering from him and covered him with a cloak.
verses.19: And he said to her, “Please give me some water, for I am thirsty.” So she opened the jar of milk, poured it out, and gave it to him.
verses.20: And he said to her, “Stand at the entrance of the tent. If anyone comes and asks you, say that there is no one here.”
verses.21: And Ya’el took the staff of his brother, placed it in his hand, and went into the cave. He inserted the staff into its socket, then landed on the ground. But he fell and died.
verses.22: And behold, the storm was chasing after Sisera. She rushed out to call for help. She said to him, “Go and see the man you are looking for.” He came to her. And behold, Sisera was dead, and the storm had passed.
verses.23: And on that day, God made the king of Canaan subject to the children of Israel.
verses.24: And the hands of the Israelites went forth, and they suffered greatly at the hands of Jabin, the king of Canaan, until they destroyed him.
